headline: 17 addresses catalogued across Ethereum, Base, BNB Chain and Avalanche; Polygon yielded none. 1 treasury Safe, 4 factory/token deployments per chain, BKN v1/v2 tokens and a staking pool.

findings.text: Fetched the Etherscan page for the Safe tagged 'Brickken: Treasury', which also shows a 'Brickken: Deployer' tag. No searchHandler or per-chain explorer name-tag searches were fetched (tool budget exhausted); other chains were covered through the official docs instead.

The Brickken API docs page for get-network-info embeds a 'Supported Networks & Addresses' block listing Factory, BKN, USDT and USDC addresses for Ethereum, Base, BNB Chain and Avalanche (plus Sepolia and Base Sepolia sandbox). Set as deployed_contracts_doc.

The CertiK Skynet page was fetched. It shows one audit (delivered 2022-12-23, 13 files, including UpgradeableBeaconEscrow.sol and UpgradeableBeaconToken.sol) and truncated BKN addresses on eth and bsc. It lists no full scope address table. The OpenZeppelin BKN v2 audit (2025-09-24, scope Brickken.sol and Migrator.sol) is cited by the migration announcement; the PDF itself was not fetched.
No GitHub repo is recorded for the protocol. The migration announcement names Brickken/bkn-2.0 at commit 68e802a as the audited repo, but it was not fetched, so no deployment artifacts were walked.
Per-chain results: Ethereum 11 addresses, Base 2, BNB Chain 2, Avalanche 2, Polygon 0. Polygon is listed in the pinned chains and in the website FAQ, but the docs' address block has no Polygon entry.

Factory addresses were found on Ethereum, Base, BNB Chain and Avalanche. Child enumeration was not performed: these addresses came from non-defipunkd sources, so the read-API surfacers were not allowlisted, and fetch budget ran out. The docs say the factory whitelists signers and the tokenizer deploys per-issuer tokens, so the child set is likely large and per-issuer.

Roles assigned from the controlled vocabulary: factory, token, treasury/multisig, pool (staking), other. Treasury actor_class is multisig on the basis of Etherscan's 'Smart Account by Safe' label and the GnosisSafeProxy source; owners and threshold were not read.
Every address in admin_addresses traces to a fetched URL in evidence[]. Snippet-only sightings are listed in unknowns[] under D8.

rationale.verdict: Discovery slice, so grade is unknown by design: walked the Brickken docs, the BKN migration announcement, the CertiK Skynet page and the Etherscan treasury page, and catalogued 17 addresses over 4 of 5 chains (Polygon had none).

evidence.shows: Probe: protocol website fetched successfully. Describes tokenization on Ethereum, Binance Smart Chain, Base and Polygon, links to docs.brickken.com, and names the BKN token page.

Official docs: per-chain Factory/BKN/USDT/USDC addresses for Ethereum (chain 1), Base (hex 2105 = 8453, derived), BNB Chain (hex 38 = 56, derived) and Avalanche (hex a86a = 43114, derived), plus Sepolia sandbox. No Polygon entry.
Docs index. Lists endpoints get-network-info, get-tokenizer-info and the ERC-8004 / ERC-8226 RAMS agentic API (Base, Ethereum Sepolia). No mainnet address page was found in it.

Official announcement: new BKN contract 0xFc209EeBA3D744aA741cc5C2A73Ebf9C977B5F82, previous BKN contract 0x0a638f07acc6969abf392bb009f216d22adea36d, official staking pool 0x8F523d7e1acbBc6D0E3CA19B7D8C1981B346ceb8 (all Ethereum). Also names the OpenZeppelin audit of Brickken.sol and Migrator.sol (2025-09-24, repo Brickken/bkn-2.0 commit 68e802a).

Public name tag 'Brickken: Treasury'; GnosisSafeProxy with Safe Singleton 1.3.0 implementation 0xd9Db270c1B5E3Bd161E8c8503c55cEABeE709552, created via Safe Proxy Factory 0xa6B71E26C5e0845f74c812102Ca7114b6a896AB2. Creator tagged 'Brickken: Deployer' 0x4413140CC8CEB93E80c0cD438aE6321D4e6ac84D. Recent execTransaction senders include the Deployer, edwinmata.eth (0x581893c06497a67642d803f114bd1f3eb5bd7fd6), 0x715aCC4a912f979279b9B3d3a46A3cF1e006C033 and 0x4fe01B97078f0f5E355bDb862da8036c1d07BA61. The senders are derived as probable signers; owners were not read.

CertiK audit delivered 2022-12-23 with 15 findings, including 3 acknowledged High centralization issues; audited files include UpgradeableBeaconEscrow.sol and UpgradeableBeaconToken.sol. Lists BKN contracts on eth (0x0ab...0c39f) and bsc (0x0e28...55b498, plus a truncated 0xc1e...c57fa). Full BSC BKN address 0x0e28bc9b03971e95acf9ae1326e51ecf9c55b498 linked to bscscan. Shows no CertiK or third-party bug bounty.
Fetched as a candidate discovery source: a media and press registry with no contract addresses.

unknowns: D1: etherscan.io/searchHandler and per-chain explorer name-tag searches (basescan.org, bscscan.com, snowtrace.io, polygonscan.com) were not fetched; the fetch budget was spent on docs and the Etherscan treasury page. A bscscan search result tagged 0x0e28bC9B... 'Brickken: Old BKN Token', but that page was not fetched.

D3: the OpenZeppelin BKN v2 audit PDF (linked in the announcement) and the CertiK audit PDF were not opened, so no scope address table was extracted. The Migrator contract address is therefore unknown.

D4: no GitHub repo is pinned. Brickken/bkn-2.0 (commit 68e802a) is named in the announcement but was not fetched, and no broadcast or deployments artifacts were walked. protocol_metadata.github is left empty.
D5: chain Polygon: zero addresses surfaced from the website, the docs get-network-info page, the CertiK page and the announcement.

D6: factory children not enumerated for Ethereum 0x91af681C85Ca98Efc5D69C1B62E6F435030969Db, Base 0x278D7bdc2451B0Fa4087A68ce084a86cB91D4d83, BNB Chain 0xCe4529Fe88df480BD777d3e32dfD7032e6C685ff or Avalanche 0xc6c230FA8F40022dE997727436Fae01caAbcDe61. The docs expose no allPools/getToken enumeration view, and surfacer URLs were not allowlisted. Per-issuer token contracts are expected to be numerous and need dedicated ingestion.

D6: a defipunkd /api/safe/owners fetch for the treasury Safe was rejected by the allowlist, because the address came from a non-defipunkd source. Treasury owners and threshold are unread; the next run can fetch them from the inherited address.

D8: snippet-only, not recorded as admin_addresses: bscscan 'Old BKN Token' label for 0x0e28bC9B... (the address itself is in the docs); the truncated CertiK BSC contract 0xc1e...c57fa (full address unknown); the truncated CertiK Ethereum address 0x0ab...0c39f (probably the old BKN 0x0A638F07..., not verified); the Etherscan-search snippet that lists 0x0a638f07... as the old BKN.
D8: the new BKN token page and the staking pool Etherscan pages were not fetched. Their addresses are cited only from the official announcement and are unverified on-chain.
D7: actor_class values for the deployer and the three Safe executor addresses are unknown. Bytecode was not read, and whether the executors are Safe owners was not read.

D7: USDT/USDC addresses listed in the docs are third-party tokens and were deliberately not catalogued. Treasury-held tokens ASSET and ISD (0x99e980265bf36516c442be982df1772a6ccb3233, 0x147b7526a66c9188ae97715da3299691db2da2b4) were seen in the Etherscan holdings list but their relation to Brickken is unverified, so they are not catalogued.
D3: upgradeability is not set. The CertiK audited file names suggest beacon-upgradeable token and escrow contracts, but no deployed proxy or implementation was read, so the value stays unknown.
D2: no governance forum, security contact or bug bounty page was found. The tech@brickken.com contact in the docs is for API-key requests, not security disclosure. CertiK shows no bug bounty.
D1: the Etherscan Treasury page shows a 'Multichain Info' XDC entry for the same Safe address; XDC is not in the pinned chains and was not investigated.

protocol_metadata.about: Brickken is a tokenization platform where companies issue and manage security tokens for real-world assets such as equity, debt, funds and real estate. Issuers use a factory contract on each supported chain to deploy per-asset tokens. A whitelisted tokenizer signer controls minting, investor whitelisting and dividend distribution, and the platform adds KYC/KYB, offerings (STOs) and an investor portal. The BKN utility token is used for platform fees and staking, and the platform has recently added an API/CLI/MCP layer for AI-agent workflows.
